name: Policyholder — three shapes
description: One classified field catalog, projected three ways: a normalised system of record, a denormalised read model, and a minimal model.

steps.title: One catalog, three shapes
steps.body: PHOLD has 288,406 records and 51 fields worth modelling. They are classified once — by what kind of thing they are, what a dashboard can do with them, and how sensitive they are — and the three shapes are projections of that one catalog. A field cannot mean different things in different shapes.

steps.title: 01 · Normalised — the system of record
steps.body: One party document with seven nested sections, plus three collections beside it. A concept earns its own collection only if a batch rebuilds it on a different cadence, or it is a security boundary. Portfolio and claims are rebuilt nightly from other files; payment instruments are isolated because they need their own lock.
questions: Should payment instruments migrate at all, or stay with the processor?

steps.title: 02 · Denormalised — what the dashboard reads
steps.body: One document per holder carrying every tile in a single fetch. Payment data is excluded outright, and anything that is drill-down rather than a tile stays on the normalised side.

steps.title: 03 · Minimal — the first dashboard
steps.body: Three collections: who they are and the dimensions every tile slices by, what they are worth, and what they cost. A field earns its place only if a tile shows it or slices by it — and most of what remains is owned by another file, so this shape cannot be built from PHOLD alone.
